commit_message: feat(ml): flavor model suite

feat(ml): scaffold-honest GNN eval + expanded odor dataset

Measurement-correctness fixes to the multitask MPNN training/eval, plus
an expanded odor-label dataset that lifts the weak odor heads.

Methodology:
- Scaffold splitting (Bemis-Murcko): GroupKFold + DeepChem-style balanced
  scaffold split (mega-scaffolds pinned to train) for out-of-scaffold
  generalization instead of homologous-series leakage across folds.
- Validation-epoch selection: replace best-epoch-on-test (F1 inflation)
  with lowest masked val-loss epoch; one model, one epoch, no per-task
  test argmax.
- Cosine LR + early-stopping(patience) to stabilize the val-loss curve.
- Held-out threshold calibration (--heldout): sweep on one test half,
  report F1 on the other, removing calibration-on-test leakage.
- readout lever in MPNN (mean / mean_max / mean_max_sum); mean_max banked
  as new default (recovers sweet, durable sour win, no head damaged).
- Word-boundary odor-keyword matching in build_compounds.

Data:
- Leffingwell odor set (3,522 molecules, 113 descriptors) mapped to the 6
  odor heads; compounds_p3b.parquet (combined) + compounds_p3b_trainonly
  .parquet (train-only confirmation). Odor-observed molecules 1,383 ->
  4,645. Rigorous train-only test: 5/6 odor heads improve (floral +0.12,
  fatty +0.14); odor_woody regresses -0.157 (vocab conflict, follow-up).

Removes flavor-gnn/src/eval/cross_validate.py (CV logic absorbed into
train_multitask.cross_validate).

commit_message:
fix(ml): exclude woody from Leffingwell odor merge (resolve -0.157 regression)

odor_woody was the one head that regressed (-0.157) when Leffingwell data
was merged. Diagnosed three compounding causes on the data:

1. Vocabulary disagreement: Leffingwell maps only {earthy,pine,smoky,woody}
   to woody, while our FlavorDB woody also counts nutty + mushroom. 19% of
   our 432 woody positives are woody ONLY via nutty/mushroom — labels
   Leffingwell explicitly calls NOT woody.
2. Prior shift: woody positive rate is 31% in our data vs 11% in the
   Leffingwell augment, dragging the model's woody prior down -> recall
   collapse on the test set.
3. Exact-match mapping gap: ingest uses `dl in kws`, so Leffingwell's
   `balsamic` descriptor never reaches woody (keyword is `balsam`),
   sparsifying the augment woody set further.

Fix: LEFFINGWELL_EXCLUDE = {"woody"} in both ingest scripts. Woody keeps its
original labels (existing rows untouched) and is left unobserved (mask=0) on
net-new augment rows, so Leffingwell adds zero woody signal. The 5 agreeing
odor heads still merge and keep their lifts. Regenerated parquets confirm
augment woody = 0/0, original woody = 432/1383 unchanged.

Re-run the 5-seed train-only scaffold eval to confirm woody returns to its
~0.517 baseline.

commit_message:
@
feat(flavor-gnn): molecular-model investigation — honest measurement, GAT, ingredient-level reality check

Concludes the flavor-model improvement campaign. Authoritative record:
flavor-gnn/artifacts/MODEL_INVESTIGATION_SUMMARY_2026-06-10.md (supersedes
contradicting forward-looking claims in older docs; banners added).

Measurement infrastructure (the lasting value):
- P0 gate: DeepChem balanced-scaffold CV (benzene pinned to train), held-out
  threshold calibration, validation-epoch selection — exposed that old CV F1 was
  inflated (scaffold leakage + calibration-on-test + best-epoch-on-test).
- Paired-control pattern (--no-augment-train): the key tool; caught a phantom
  P3b "win" that cross-test-set comparison had manufactured.

Model levers (all paired-measured): GAT backbone is the only real win (floral
+0.058); readout-beyond-mean_max, odor de-noise, external odor data (P3b),
physchem descriptors all flat-to-negative; chirality untestable (0.5% stereo SMILES).

Key finding: molecular odor F1 does NOT survive compound->ingredient aggregation
(chef ingredient AUROC ~0.5; odor ingredient F1 ~0). Validated against the Flavor
Bible (25,844 curated pairs): GNN profiles predict pairings at only ~0.58 AUROC.
=> The molecular profile is a visualization tool, not a culinary-signal tool.
Recommendation: pairings come from curated graphs (RecipeNLG co-occurrence + the
Flavor Bible), not the molecular model.

Adds: backbone/readout/descriptor/stereo options to the GNN; scaffold-split eval;
Leffingwell ingestion (gated); Flavor Bible name-matcher (9%->46%,
flavor_bible_matched.json, 9,557 pairs); processed-food manifest; doc reconciliation.

commit_message:
feat(pairing): Flavor Bible curated pairing layer (set-intersection)

Adds The Flavor Bible's curated pairings as a third high-reliability
signal in the affinity layer, complementary to RecipeNLG co-occurrence
and molecular bridge compounds. Direct set-intersection (like the
reference app areeves87/Flavor-Bible-App match_up), NOT model-predicted
pairings — the molecular GNN's ~0.58 pairing AUROC is why we use the
curated graph directly rather than predicting from the flavor profile.
No molecular-model code touched; GNN profile stays visualization-only.

Data (FB-PAIR-1): match_flavor_bible_v2.py now persists the matched
graph. Ships the PRECISE 8,270-pair / 449-ingredient set (equality-based
stages only); the heuristic head-noun + fuzzy stages are gated behind
--precise (off) since a false match asserts an FB endorsement that
doesn't exist — precision > recall for an authoritative layer. 0 orphans.

Layer (FB-PAIR-2/3/4): useProData builds flavorBibleSet (canonical-keyed)
+ flavorBibleNeighbors adjacency. tierFor floors FB pairs at ★★ with an
fb provenance flag; topAffinities walks FB adjacency so the ~82% of FB
pairs with no corpus edge (the canonical-but-corpus-missed ones — the
whole point) surface in α-mode (thyme +76, basil +55, almond +80).
Purely additive: empty/absent set → identical to prior behavior.

Surfaces (FB-PAIR-5): 📖 badge in AffinityPanel, IngredientPanel rows,
PairingModeCard. FB-only pairs surface as new candidates in α-mode only;
the two corpus-edge-based list surfaces badge the corpus-overlap subset
(full FB-only surfacing there is a documented follow-up).

Tests: +6 affinityTiers cases (floor, fb flag, order-independence,
FB-walk, null-safe baseline). Full suite 1256/1256, build clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(recipe): wire smart recipe creator — set-completion + quantity

Makes the built-but-unwired FM-P2 set-completion model (Flow A: "user
picked a few → suggest the rest", cuisine-aware) a live feature, plus
FM-Q2 quantity auto-fill.

Surfacing: a distinct "✨ Smart completions" group above the existing
co-occurrence list in IngredientSuggestionsPopout (add mode). The model
beat the popularity baseline on held-out reconstruction (hit@10 0.866 vs
0.799), so it earns a labeled group — unlike the pairing model which
lost to co-occurrence and is NOT used for ranking. Cuisine is
auto-derived from the bowl (deriveBowlCuisine → model cuisine_vocab).

Discovery: the popout was orphaned by the 2026-06-03 B-version refactor
(mount removed, but RecipeNotebook's "Suggestions…" button still set
suggestionsMode → rendered nothing — a dead button). Re-mounted the
smart-enhanced popout on suggestionsMode in RecipeLabMobile: ships the
feature on the live surface AND fixes the dead button.

Quantity: tapping any suggestion prefills an editable amount via the
FM-Q2 model. Prediction is synchronous (preload the artifact on mount,
predict from cache) so onAdd still fires immediately — preserving the
add contract and all prior popout tests. amount is threaded through
handleAddIngredient → bowlAddIngredient; 2nd arg only when predicted.

Artifacts: quantity_model.json shipped to public/models (reuses the
byte-identical recipe_vocab.json vocab). recipe-setcompletion.onnx +
recipe_vocab.json already shipped. Flag FN_RECIPE_MODEL (default ON,
localStorage escape); purely additive — flag-off / load-fail / no vocab
match → co-occurrence list unchanged.

Tests: +7 deriveBowlCuisine cases; existing popout suite green. Full
1271/1271, build clean.

commit_message:
test(ml): Flow-B contrastive decoding — measured NEGATIVE, do not ship

Tests the feasibility doc's top Flow-B lever ("popularity discounting")
as contrastive decoding: score(i|P) = logit(i|P) − α·logit(i|baseline),
baseline = empty observed + zero profile. No retrain, two model passes,
in-browser-portable.

Result: contrastive monotonically LOWERS profile fidelity as α rises
(α0=0.594 → α0.5=0.575 → α1.0=0.490 → α1.5=0.426). The low pairwise
overlap it buys (0.307→0.010) is a proxy-metric trap — high α promotes
rare ingredients (low baseline logit) that merely differ from staples
without matching the target ("dessert → pork shoulder, vinegar, brussels
sprout"). Profile fidelity is the honest quality metric and it says the
lever strictly hurts.

Root cause: the averaged 11-D gnn_entropy profile isn't a discriminative
conditioning signal; contrastive can demote the staple prior but can't
synthesize an on-target set. Same theme as the rest of the campaign —
discrete seed ingredients are the strong instrument (Flow A works),
abstract profile conditioning doesn't.

Decision: Flow-B (profile-only generation) stays UNSHIPPED; generation
stays seeded by ingredients + cuisine (Flow A, already live). Levers #2/#3
require a retrain and aren't justified by measured value. Infra retained
for cheap future re-measurement (like the DREAM/focal dead-ends).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ml): FM-DIR1 directions via retrieval (capability, not wired)

Given a recipe bowl (ingredient-name set), retrieve the most set-similar
real RecipeNLG recipes and return their verbatim cooking directions —
grounded, no generation, fully in-browser. Per feasibility doc §11.4
this is a CAPABILITY (runtime + index + tests); UI wiring is a follow-up.

Index (flavor-gnn/scripts/fm_dir1_build_index.mjs): streams the 2.2GB
RecipeNLG CSV joined to recipe_sets.jsonl (verified 7/7 row-alignment,
r = 0-based CSV data-row index, no offset). 40k deduped recipes,
nm∈[3,10], → public/models/directions_index.json (14.4MB uncompressed,
2.69MB brotli in build). Inverted index (vocab_id → recipe idxs) for
fast candidate gathering. Coverage: 2,082/3,891 vocab ids (capped at
first 40k; widening the cap is a documented follow-up).

Runtime (src/ml/directionsRuntime.js): lazy null-safe loader + pure,
unit-tested retrieveDirections (Jaccard over vocab-id sets via the
inverted index, minOverlap gate) + adaptSteps (returns real steps
verbatim + present/absent provenance lists — no risky rewriting).

Smoke: [flour,butter,sugar,egg,vanilla] → Texas Prize Cake (J=1.0);
[soy sauce,ginger,garlic,scallion] → Szechuan Steak / fried rice.

onnxruntime-web 1.24's default backend loads the JSEP variant
(ort-wasm-simd-threaded.jsep.{mjs,wasm}), but copy_wasm.cjs only copied

server responded with a MIME type of text/html". This broke the recipe
set-completion model (✨ Suggest / Smart swaps); the quantity + cooking-
method features (plain JSON fetch, no ort) were unaffected.

/wasm/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.jsep.mjs now serves text/javascript (200).

fix(app): resilient lazy chunks + mobile-web-app-capable meta

Two console-error fixes reported from the live app:

1. Deprecated <meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-capable"> warning — add the
   standard <meta name="mobile-web-app-capable" content="yes"> (keep the
   apple one for older iOS Safari).

2. "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: …/MoleculeLab-*.js"
   (ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT). The chunk is current and serves fine
   (~1s); it was a transient network blip — but a blip permanently broke
   the lazy route. New lazyWithRetry wraps React.lazy with linear-backoff
   retries, then a one-shot sessionStorage-guarded page reload to recover
   from a stale chunk after a deploy. Applied to MoleculeLab (App),
   CocktailLabV2 + SauceLab (MakeRecipeView).

(Note: the /data/*.json "timeouts" were a curl artifact — without
Accept-Encoding curl pulls the 160-250KB uncompressed file; real browsers
get the brotli variant in ~0.12s. No server fix needed.)

loadWithRetry is injectable + unit-tested (5 cases: success, retry-then-
succeed, reload-once, no-loop-when-flagged, flag-cleared-on-success).
Full suite 1310/1310, build clean.

commit_message:
fix(recipe): make ingredient suggestions actually smart

The suggest/replace feature was returning global staples (salt, sugar,
flour) regardless of recipe — e.g. pad thai → replace rice noodle → salt.
Audit (flavor-gnn/scripts/fm_p2_suggest_audit.mjs) found three causes:

1. CUISINE NEVER APPLIED. The deck/profiles card read `rt.deriveBowlCuisine`
   but recipeRuntime never exported it → cuisine always null → the model
   ran unconditioned (staple-dominated). Now import deriveBowlCuisine
   properly. Cuisine conditioning is night-and-day (pad thai → cilantro,
   lime juice, soy sauce, scallion, sesame oil, ginger, shrimp, peanut oil).

2. deriveBowlCuisine picked the WRONG cuisine entry. cuisine_vocab contains
   both a well-trained 'Thai' and a rare duplicate lowercase 'thai'; the
   lowercased lookup let the weak variant win. Now keep-first → canonical.

3. RAW ARGMAX = staples. Added a popularity discount (contrastive:
   score = logit(i|recipe) − α·logit(i|∅), α=0.3) that demotes ingredients
   the model predicts for every recipe. Baseline logits cached on the model.

Replace is now category-aware: candidates restricted to the focal's
category (rice noodle → grains) then ranked by recipe fit → real
substitutes (long-grain rice, vermicelli, somen/angel-hair/glass noodle,
pasta), not condiments. rankLogits gains a candidate-pool arg (3 tests).

SuggestionCardDeck redesigned: recipe flavor-profile radar at top + a
scrollable list of ~18 ranked suggestions, each with its profile-shift
delta and an Add/Swap action (was a one-at-a-time swipe deck).

Verified end-to-end in a real browser on a pad-thai bowl. Full suite
1312/1312, build clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
feat(recipe): exclude pantry staples + cuisine/family-aware replacements

- Exclude water, salt, pepper (incl. black pepper), sugar, flour from ALL
  ingredient suggestions (add/replace/boost/temper) — pantry staples are
  never a useful suggestion (user request). Filtered at the source in
  suggestIngredients so every surface benefits. (Red/green/bell pepper are
  vegetables — kept.)
- Replace re-rank: prioritize substitutes whose PRIMARY cuisine matches the
  recipe's dominant cuisine / region (using the primary cuisine, not the
  noisily-tagged full list), and drop Western pastas (lasagna, macaroni,
  ziti, rigatoni, penne, spaghetti) when swapping a noodle — so pad thai's
  rice noodle gets Asian noodles, not lasagna.

  gnn_compounds tag -> {t3 mouthfeel | normalized leaf | skip}. Covers
  100% of the 143 descriptors appearing in >=10 ingredients (AC >=90%).
  Audit finding 2.4: ambiguous tokens get explicit decisions instead of
  substring guesses (warm->skip, mushroom->leaf not woody, coconut->leaf
  + creamy->mouthfeel not fatty).
- derive_long_tail.py: loads the lookup for Tier-3 and noise-filtered leaf
  derivation; long-tail (<10) tags still pass through as raw leaves.
- backfill_top500_tier3.py: fills the 114 empty tier3 cells (62% -> 94%;
  leaves 94%). Empty-only, zero chef cells overwritten; provenance tagged
  t3-curated (59 hand-assigned in the chef's vocabulary) / t3-derived (37).
  18 genuinely ambiguous rows left empty.
- test_descriptor_lookup.py: coverage + skip/normalization + audit-token

feat(data): N1-D3 bake flavor_graph.json + vocabulary + wire useProData

Bakes the per-ingredient flavor graph the IngredientPanel chip-cloud
consumes, with the new vocabulary cross-check, and wires it into the app.

- bake_flavor_graph.py -> public/proDataset/flavor_graph.json with shape
  {ingredients, vocabulary, edges}. Built from flavor_graph_full.csv with
  the chef top500 overlaid (chef rows win), so chef fixes propagate without
  a destructive flavor_graph_full regen. vocabulary is derived from the
  ingredients, so the term cross-check is true by construction.
  4121 ingredients; mint = canonical fixture.
- useProData.js: loads flavor_graph.json as the authoritative chip-cloud
  tier source (full-corpus coverage + corrected fixtures), keeping
  embedding/cluster from flavor_graph_data_v3. Decoupled from
  primaryTier1Aroma so the chef-approved N1-D5 network coloring is
  unchanged. The older "89 chef rows only" comment was stale (v3 already
  carried 3,810 tiered nodes).
- top500_flavor_graph.csv: restored the canonical mint fixture (tier2
  bitter|astringent, tier3 cooling|pungent, leaves menthol|fresh|sharp|
  grassy|herbaceous) which had drifted from its documented reference, and
  fixed vanilla's mis-derived 'cooling' mouthfeel -> creamy|smooth.
- flavorGraphArtifact.test.js: shape + mint fixture + vocabulary
  cross-check. Full vitest suite green (1315); production build clean.

Acceptance: flavor_graph.json parses with ingredients+vocabulary keys;
mint canonical; every tier term in vocabulary; 84% of top-500 are 4-of-4;
useProData loads it.

commit_message:
feat(data): LLM-distilled ingredient-level flavor profiles + IngredientPanel surfacing

Re-sources the ingredient-level odor/taste signal the 2026-06-10 model
investigation named as the binding constraint (molecular GNN F1 doesn't
survive compound->ingredient aggregation; chef AUROC ~0.5). Deep research
found no open ingredient-level dataset at scale — all candidates are
molecule-keyed, paywalled, or too small — so the signal is distilled with
expert-anchored LLM labeling instead.

Pipeline (flavor-gnn/scripts/pilot_odor_labels/):
- Calibration pilot, blind-labeled vs the 304-row chef gold set. v1
  (single primary aroma) hit 11-head macro-F1 0.606; v2 (multi-label aroma
  vs the leaves-derived gold + salty/umami + spicy/pungent boundary rubric)
  hit 0.710 vs the molecular model's 0.101 (~7x).
- Full-corpus distillation: 3-sample blind consensus (>=2 of 3) over all
  3,624 non-chef ingredients, chef rows overlaid by precedence. Output:
  public/proDataset/flavor_profiles_distilled.json (3,927 profiles; 0
  invalid/empty/out-of-vocab; salty + odor_spicy flagged low_confidence,
  matching the molecular model's known-weak axes).

UI:
- useProData attaches node.distilledProfile from the new JSON.
- DistilledProfile.jsx renders aroma + taste chips, dimming/dashing
  low_confidence axes; mounted as a "Flavor profile" section (open) above
  the now-secondary "Molecular Profile" in both IngredientPanel paths.

Full suite green (1315 tests incl. new DistilledProfile.test.jsx), build clean.
Decision record: flavor-gnn/artifacts/INGREDIENT_ODOR_LABEL_SOURCING_2026-06-13.md.
Bulky regenerable batch/pred intermediates gitignored.

Lesson harvest: clean (no gate failures this task).

commit_message:
docs(spike): FP-OV-4 — local ONNX flavor-description model feasibility (NO-GO)

Feasibility spike for replacing/augmenting the FP-OV-2 rule-based flavor
description with a LOCAL onnxruntime-web model (no cloud API). Verdict: NO-GO.

- Platform is proven: the app already runs onnxruntime-web (WASM, single-thread,
  SIMD) in-browser and in Capacitor iOS WKWebView with 0.5 MB + 4.18 MB models.
- Off-the-shelf generative floor (flan-t5-small) is ~94 MB int8 (~22x the
  set-completion model), multi-second single-thread WASM decode, and risks iOS
  WKWebView OOM.
- Decisive argument (size-independent): the only training signal is the FP-OV-2
  rule output, so any learned model — tiny or large — has the rules as its
  quality ceiling while adding hallucination risk on short factual text.
- Cheaper future lever for richer prose: expand the FP-OV-2 rule templates,
  not an in-browser LM.

No follow-up implementation task appended (the "if go" branch does not fire).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
